situation: Mime is offered with five public Steel cards and full Joker slots.
options: Reroll and keep the current five Jokers.
Sell a replaceable Joker, reobserve, then consider Mime.
lesson: Mime can retrigger held Steel effects; surface the engine even when capacity makes purchase a separate later action.
reversal: Keep the current build when reliable output or economy matters more than draw-dependent held Steel.

situation: A free Hanging Chad is offered while Justice and enhanced scoring cards are public.
options: Skip and preserve the mature Joker lineup.
Sell, reobserve, and consider Chad for a first-card retrigger line.
lesson: Chad retriggers the first scoring card twice, so supported Glass or other scoring-card effects can justify a build transition.
reversal: Skip when no suitable first scoring card is available or the displaced Joker is essential for survival.

situation: Baron is offered with five public Kings, including a red-seal Steel King.
options: Reroll for a less draw-dependent upgrade.
Sell, reobserve, and consider Baron as held-card scaling.
lesson: Count public Kings and relevant seals before presenting Baron; multiple Kings make its held XMult route plausible, not guaranteed.
reversal: Decline when hand size, draw reliability, or a strong additive Joker makes holding Kings impractical.

situation: Constellation at X1 is offered beside an established Baseball engine and visible Planet plans.
options: Keep current flat Mult and interest.
Transition to an uncommon scaler and fund future Planet use.
lesson: Constellation starts weak but is uncommon for Baseball and grows on Planet use; treat it as a conditional investment.
reversal: Pass when there is no Planet budget or immediate scoring cannot absorb an X1 scaler.

situation: Hologram at X1 is offered with Baseball and a visible pattern of opening card-adding packs.
options: Reroll and retain current scoring.
Replace a flat Joker and commit to adding useful cards.
lesson: Hologram is an uncommon Baseball target and grows when cards are added, but X1 alone is not an immediate scoring upgrade.
reversal: Pass when added cards would dilute the deck or there is no budget to grow Hologram.

situation: Ramen is offered after the build has stabilized and can reduce discretionary discards.
options: Keep Cloud 9 income and Holographic Mult.
Sell Cloud 9, reobserve, then buy Ramen for XMult.
lesson: Ramen begins at X2 and loses X0.01 per discarded card; buying it should change later discard discipline.
reversal: Keep economy when survival still depends on frequent discards or the lost income funds stronger upgrades.

situation: A red-seal Steel card is public when Mime is offered.
options: Build around holding the sealed Steel card.
Keep playing it when its rank or hand shape is more valuable.
lesson: Mime retriggers held-card abilities and a red seal adds a card repetition; confirm the card can remain held.
reversal: Abandon the line when forced selection, debuff, or hand-size pressure prevents holding it.

situation: Baron is offered with only the normal or low public King count.
options: Buy and begin a King-duplication plan.
Prefer a reliable multiplier already supported by the deck.
lesson: Baron gives X1.5 for each held King, but low King density makes the payoff draw-dependent.
reversal: Take Baron when duplication, hand size, or a held-card retrigger already makes the direction coherent.

situation: Baron and Mime share a held-King or Steel plan.
options: Add more Baron-style held XMult.
Add more held-card repetitions through Mime or a copier.
lesson: Balance effect count against retrigger count using the cards actually held; neither Joker is universally the better copy target.
reversal: Favor the side that is currently scarcer after counting held effects, seals, and copy placement.

situation: Stuntman supplies chips while a held-card engine needs room for Kings or Steel.
options: Keep Stuntman for reliable chips.
Replace it to restore hand size for more held effects.
lesson: A held-card build should price Stuntman's hand-size reduction against its dependable chip contribution.
reversal: Keep Stuntman when chips are the bottleneck or the deck cannot reliably fill added held slots.

situation: A Glass face can be placed first among scoring cards with Photograph and Chad active.
options: Lead with the Glass face for repeated effects.
Preserve Glass and use a safer scoring card.
lesson: Glass gives X2, Photograph can give X2 on the first scoring face, and Chad repeats the first scoring card twice.
reversal: Avoid the line when the score is already sufficient or losing Glass would damage future survival.

situation: Several selected cards score, but only one has a strong enhancement or edition.
options: Place the supported card first physically.
Keep current order when another first-card effect dominates.
lesson: Chad repeats the first scoring card. Reordering the same physical cards can change the score; remap selected slots after the reorder.
reversal: Do not reorder when the candidate scorer shows no gain or a boss/order effect makes the result uncertain.

situation: Photograph is offered but the public deck has few or no face cards.
options: Buy and plan to add faces.
Pass for an engine supported by current cards.
lesson: Photograph needs the first played face card to score; its label alone is not evidence of reliable XMult.
reversal: Take it when face density, copying, or retriggers make a deliberate face-scoring plan credible.

situation: Blueprint can be positioned to copy Hanging Chad in a played-card engine.
options: Copy Chad for more first-card repetitions.
Copy a main multiplier instead.
lesson: Copy placement should follow the current scoring card and multiplier chain, not a fixed target rule.
reversal: Copy the main multiplier when first-card effects are weak, debuffed, or absent from the play.

situation: Brainstorm is owned with several compatible engines in different Joker positions.
options: Move the desired target to the leftmost slot.
Leave order when the current target is better.
lesson: Brainstorm copies the leftmost Joker if that Joker is compatible; it does not search onward for a compatible target.
reversal: Do not reorder when hidden Jokers or a boss prevents a reliable public comparison.

situation: Blueprint's immediate right neighbor changed after a purchase or boss shuffle.
options: Reorder toward the intended compatible target.
Keep order and accept the current target.
lesson: Blueprint copies the compatible Joker to its right; purchases and shuffles require a fresh target check.
reversal: Skip automatic reordering when the target is hidden or scorer coverage is unavailable.

situation: A face card can be selected as a non-scoring kicker while a numbered card forms the scoring hand.
options: Use the face only as a harmless kicker.
Choose a play where the face scores.
lesson: Ride the Bus resets on a scoring face; distinguish scoring cards from selected kickers.
reversal: Treat safety as uncertain with unsupported interactions or when Splash makes every selected card score.

situation: Shortcut or Four Fingers can make a Straight plan easier to draw.
options: Buy consistency and invest in Straight levels.
Keep a more reliable small-hand engine.
lesson: Shortcut permits rank gaps; Four Fingers reduces the required Straight length to four. Check the actual rank spread before committing.
reversal: Pass when the deck still cannot draw Straights reliably or the slot must supply immediate score.

situation: A play leaves only Spades and Clubs in hand.
options: Play off-colour cards to activate Blackboard.
Keep a valuable red-suit held card and lose Blackboard.
lesson: Blackboard gives X3 when every held card is a Spade or Club; evaluate the actual cards left behind.
reversal: Keep the red-suit card when its Steel, seal, or future value outweighs current Blackboard XMult.

situation: A suit-changing consumable can turn red-suit cards into Spades or Clubs for Blackboard.
options: Edit suits toward a more reliable held-black condition.
Use the consumable for another hand or save it.
lesson: Deck edits can improve Blackboard reliability, but a visible target and legal phase are required.
reversal: Avoid the edit when it breaks a stronger flush, suit, or boss plan.

situation: Runner has accumulated chips, but the deck is becoming less reliable at making Straights.
options: Keep playing Straights to continue growth.
Preserve the banked chips and pivot the hand plan.
lesson: Runner keeps its accumulated chips; future growth requires playing another Straight.
reversal: Keep committing when Straight consistency and hand levels remain the best route.

situation: Ancient Joker names a suit that the current public hand or deck may not support.
options: Build the scoring hand around the named suit.
Use a reliable hand and forgo its trigger.
lesson: Ancient Joker rewards scoring cards of its current suit, so judge the visible suit rather than generic Flush strength.
reversal: Follow the target when enough scoring cards of that suit are available without breaking the hand.

situation: Bloodstone is supported by visible Hearts, but its scoring-card triggers are random.
options: Play a Heart-heavy scoring hand.
Choose the steadier available line.
lesson: Bloodstone gives scoring Hearts a chance to add X1.5 Mult; treat the payoff as stochastic rather than guaranteed.
reversal: Prefer the steady line when the blind cannot tolerate a missed trigger.

situation: A Standard Pack can add a card while Hologram is owned.
options: Add a useful card and grow Hologram.
Skip a weak card to protect deck consistency.
lesson: Hologram grows when a playing card is added, but growth does not make every offered card a good deck edit.
reversal: Add the card when its rank, enhancement, seal, or edition supports the main engine.

situation: A Planet for the main hand is available while Constellation is owned.
options: Use it for both hand level and Constellation growth.
Save money or choose a different pack card.
lesson: Planet use grows Constellation by X0.1 and can also level the relevant hand; verify the Planet matches the actual build.
reversal: Skip when economy or a stronger pack choice outweighs the combined incremental growth.

situation: No discard has been used this round and Burnt Joker can level the first discarded poker hand.
options: Discard the hand family intended for leveling.
Save the discard for draw quality.
lesson: Burnt Joker levels only the first discarded poker hand each round, so the first discard determines its growth target.
reversal: Use the discard for survival when shaping the named hand would make the round unsafe.

situation: Several legal plays clear, but only one names the hand intended for long-term leveling.
options: Play the target family and hold the Blue Seal.
Take the higher immediate score from another family.
lesson: Blue Seal value depends on the hand actually played; align it with the build rather than any sufficient hand.
reversal: Choose immediate score when the target-family line risks losing the blind.

situation: Card Sharp is active after the same poker hand has already been played this round.
options: Repeat the family for X3 Mult.
Change family for a stronger base hand or boss constraint.
lesson: Card Sharp gives X3 only after that poker hand was already played this round; first-hand and repeat-hand scores differ.
reversal: Change families when the repeated hand is illegal, debuffed, or cannot meet the target.

situation: A discard advances Yorick toward its next permanent XMult increase, but also spends draw control.
options: Advance Yorick with a safe discard.
Keep the discard for hand completion.
lesson: Yorick rewards a cumulative number of discarded cards; progress can be deferred when the current round needs draw control.
reversal: Spend the discard when the remaining hands and deck make the clear secure.

situation: Ramen is active and a discard could improve the next hand.
options: Avoid the discard and preserve XMult.
Discard because draw quality or survival is worth X0.01.
lesson: Ramen loses X0.01 per discarded card, so discard value must exceed a visible persistent scoring cost.
reversal: Discard freely when the current hand cannot clear or the better draw protects the run.

situation: A relevant Joker is visible but all normal Joker slots are occupied.
options: Sell a chosen Joker, settle, then reassess the offer.
Keep the lineup and preserve money.
lesson: A full slot hides an immediate buy action, not the strategic offer; selling and buying are separate decisions with a fresh observation.
reversal: Do not sell when the offer may disappear, capacity is uncertain, or the current Joker is needed for the next blind.

situation: A visible Jack can be discarded for Hit the Road during the current round.
options: Discard the Jack for temporary XMult.
Keep it for the scoring hand or future draw shape.
lesson: Hit the Road gains XMult for discarded Jacks and resets after the round, so this is a current-round payoff.
reversal: Keep the Jack when it is essential to the scoring hand or the temporary gain is unnecessary.

situation: Buying a supported scaler would cross an interest threshold.
options: Preserve the economy floor.
Spend now for a coherent scoring transition.
lesson: Compare known interest loss with the engine's conditions and next-blind need; neither saving nor spending is universally correct.
reversal: Preserve cash when the offer starts inactive or the current build already clears comfortably.

situation: The visible Plant debuffs face cards while the build uses Photograph or held Kings.
options: Reroll or adapt away from faces.
Proceed if non-face engines still clear.
lesson: The Plant can suppress a face engine; evaluate Photograph or Baron with the visible boss rather than deck counts alone.
reversal: Keep the engine when the boss is disabled or other scoring layers make the blind safe.

situation: A Planet matches the hand repeatedly used by Card Sharp and the current plan.
options: Level the established hand.
Choose economy, deck editing, or a speculative family.
lesson: Concentrating levels in the hand actually played improves its base before later multiplier effects.
reversal: Diversify when a boss blocks the main family or the deck has clearly transitioned to another hand.

situation: Smeared Joker can make red or black cards cooperate in Flush hands.
options: Build around easier Flush draws.
Keep the slot for score and pursue another hand.
lesson: Smeared treats Hearts and Diamonds as one suit, and Spades and Clubs as one suit. Consistency alone does not supply scaling.
reversal: Pass when Flush levels and scoring support are weak or a visible suit-debuff boss undermines the plan.

situation: Castle names a discard suit, and cards of that suit are visible.
options: Discard matching cards to add chips.
Save them for the scoring hand.
lesson: Castle gains chips only from discarded cards of its current suit; check the visible target before spending a discard.
reversal: Keep matching cards when they are needed to form the winning hand.

situation: Perkeo can copy a held consumable when leaving the shop.
options: Hold the consumable and leave to copy it.
Use or sell it before leaving.
lesson: On leaving the shop, Perkeo randomly copies one held consumable as Negative; manage the possible targets. Negative copies bypass normal capacity.
reversal: Use the original first when its immediate effect is more valuable than another copy.

situation: DNA or Death can duplicate a rank already central to a Five of a Kind plan.
options: Copy the supported rank or enhanced card.
Preserve hand economy and current consistency.
lesson: DNA copies a single-card first hand; Death converts one selected card into another, so target identity and order matter.
reversal: Do not force duplication when the setup hand risks the blind or the target cannot be selected legally.

situation: Face cards can score with Triboulet, Sock and Buskin, or Photograph visible.
options: Build a face-scoring retrigger chain.
Retain a non-face engine resistant to face debuffs.
lesson: Triboulet gives scoring Kings and Queens X2; Sock retriggers faces; Photograph rewards the first scoring face.
reversal: Pivot when face density is low or face debuffs disable the engine; hidden cards add uncertainty rather than automatically disabling it.

situation: Money is near Vagabond’s threshold before a scoring hand.
options: Stay at or below the threshold to create Tarot.
Keep or earn more money for shop economy.
lesson: Vagabond creates a Tarot after a scoring hand only when money is at or below its threshold and capacity allows.
reversal: Favor economy when deliberately staying poor costs more than the Tarot generation is worth.

situation: To the Moon, Rocket, or Business Card offers economy instead of immediate scoring.
options: Invest in income for later shops.
Buy scoring needed for the next blind.
lesson: To the Moon improves interest, Rocket pays and grows after bosses, and Business Card can pay on scoring faces.
reversal: Prefer immediate score when the run cannot safely wait for the economy to repay its slot and cost.

situation: Scoring 2s can trigger both Wee Joker growth and Hack retriggers.
options: Build the scoring hand around supported 2s.
Use a stronger hand without forcing low ranks.
lesson: Wee Joker gains chips from scoring 2s, while Hack retriggers ranks 2 through 5; their overlap makes public 2 density relevant.
reversal: Pivot when too few low ranks can score reliably or a boss debuffs the line.

situation: Observatory is owned and a Planet matching the played hand can remain held.
options: Hold the matching Planet for XMult.
Use it now to level the hand and free capacity.
lesson: Observatory makes a held matching Planet give X1.5; compare repeated held value with permanent hand leveling.
reversal: Use the Planet when capacity, immediate base score, or another consumable matters more.

situation: Madness is considered with Eternal Jokers or expendable slots before a non-boss blind.
options: Build a protected shell around Madness growth.
Keep several ordinary Jokers and avoid random destruction.
lesson: Madness gains XMult and destroys another Joker on Small or Big Blind selection; Eternal status changes the destruction risk.
reversal: Pass when key non-Eternal Jokers cannot be protected or upcoming growth opportunities are too few.

situation: Midas Mask and Vampire can interact on scoring face cards, but Joker order controls whether new Gold is consumed immediately.
options: Order Midas before Vampire for same-play feeding.
Order Vampire before Midas to leave new Gold cards.
lesson: Midas makes scoring faces Gold; Vampire removes scoring-card enhancements for growth. Vampire removes enhancements, not seals.
reversal: Preserve Gold or another enhancement when its card value matters more than immediate Vampire growth.

situation: Two or more poker hands are tied for most played while Obelisk is owned or offered.
options: Play a hand below the tied leaders.
Skip Obelisk and continue a leading hand.
lesson: Obelisk resets on a hand tied for most played; a safe pivot must be below every current leader.
reversal: Take a leading hand when it is required to clear or no lower-count hand is reliable.

situation: Low-rank cards can support Hiker, Wee Joker, Fibonacci, or Hack.
options: Retrigger and permanently grow supported low ranks.
Favor higher ranks or another hand engine.
lesson: Hiker adds permanent chips, Wee grows from scoring 2s, Fibonacci rewards A/2/3/5/8, and Hack retriggers 2 through 5.
reversal: Pass when supported ranks are sparse, debuffed, or cannot form the chosen scoring hand.
